prompt:
A wide 16:9 landscape painting, a distant panoramic view at eye level, straight-on, layered in depth from a large foreground island to far misty hills.

Style: dark storybook ink and wash on aged sepia paper, soft wet washes, fine etched cross-hatching, mottled stains, visible paper grain, a painted vignette. Palette: soot black #171614, charcoal, umber and smoky taupe; light only as warm ivory #FFF3D6 and thin gold #E9C46A with amber #FFC76A glints; wind in muted desaturated ash blue #555E60. Grass is dry ochre-brown, flowers cream, every other tone muted brown-grey. The only lettering anywhere is the Roman numerals on the clocks; there are no people.

The left 40% of the frame, top to bottom, is an empty field of deep soot-black and charcoal mist with a few tiny gold sparks, kept open for lettering, holding no shapes, clock or frame. It fades into smoky taupe fog near the 40% line.

The right 60% holds the scene. A large rocky island fills the lower right and runs off the bottom and right edges, its top rimmed with thin gold light, its underside a ragged mass of dripping stalactites. On it stand a timber-framed cottage with a steep dark slate roof, two chimneys, ivy, a thread of white smoke and two glowing amber windows; a small lantern on a post; a wooden fence; and a wooden windmill beside it with four torn cream canvas sails. At centre-left a mid-sized island holds a tall ruined stone arch; below it a smaller island carries a low stone bridge arch. A few tiny islands drift between, and a dark island fragment is cropped at the top-right corner. Behind them, rolling misty ridges recede in layers; on the far ridges sit a small spired castle silhouette and rows of broken aqueduct arches. In the upper-right sky hang a huge ghostly clock face and a smaller one overlapping it, drawn in thin etched ink line with Roman numerals and one long pointed hand tipped in gold, half hidden by cloud, with a warm gold-ochre glow behind them, the brightest part of the picture. Long, thin, translucent ribbons of smoky ash-blue wind sweep in S-curves from the lower left up to the upper right.

Finish: keep this exact composition and value structure; the whole picture reads as a worn hand-printed etching, with coarse paper fibre and ink stipple visible at every scale, slightly rough uneven ink edges, small ink blots and scratches, and a darker overall exposure with deep soot shadows. Thin gold light only along the top edge of the foreground rock.
